language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Map and Set are standard collection types for keys/values and unique membership.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Map stores key-value associations with keys not limited to strings. Set stores unique values. WeakMap/WeakSet have object-key/value constraints and garbage-collection-oriented behavior.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: new Map(), map.set(k,v), map.get(k), new Set(), set.add(v), WeakMap
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Collection choice determines key identity, iteration order expectations, serialization, and performance shape.
common_use: Use Map for object keys or non-string keys
Use WeakMap for private metadata tied to object lifetime
common_misuse: Using plain object as map with arbitrary user keys
Expecting JSON.stringify Map/Set to preserve entries
Using WeakMap when iteration is required
safe_refactor_notes: Switch object to Map only after updating access/serialization code

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: JSON converts compatible JavaScript values to text and parses JSON text back to data.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: JSON.stringify handles objects, arrays, strings, finite numbers, booleans, and null, with special behavior for undefined, functions, symbols, Dates/toJSON, non-finite numbers, and unsupported/cyclic values. JSON.parse can use a reviver.
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: JSON is a data boundary, not a faithful snapshot of arbitrary JavaScript objects.
common_misuse: Serializing class instances, Maps, Sets, Errors, Dates, functions, undefined, cycles, or special numbers without custom logic
tests_or_checks: List non-JSON value types before boundary
safe_refactor_notes: Use explicit schema/custom serialization for non-plain data
Keep parse validation separate from parsing

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Date represents moments in time but many methods expose local or UTC views.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: Date stores a timestamp and provides constructors/parsing/formatting/accessors. Local timezone, UTC methods, string parsing, and daylight-saving transitions affect results.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: new Date(), Date.now(), Date.parse(s), date.toISOString(), date.getFullYear(), date.getUTCFullYear()
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Date bugs are common at browser/server boundaries and when local dates are treated as instants.
common_misuse: Using local getter when UTC intended
tests_or_checks: Prefer ISO with timezone for instants
safe_refactor_notes: Do not change parse/format without timezone tests
Separate date-only domain values from instants

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: Regular expressions describe text patterns for search, validation, split, and replace.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: RegExp objects and regex literals use pattern syntax plus flags. Capturing, greediness, anchors, global/sticky behavior, Unicode handling, and lastIndex can affect results.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: /pattern/flags, new RegExp(s), re.test(str), str.match(re), str.replace(re, repl)
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Regex is powerful but can overmatch, undermatch, or become unreadable when used as a parser.
common_misuse: Reusing global regex with test without considering state
safe_refactor_notes: Prefer parser/manual logic for nested formats
Avoid hidden global state in shared regex

language_semantics_records.plain_language_meaning: JavaScript reports exceptional failures through thrown values, commonly Error objects.
language_semantics_records.precise_behavior: throw transfers control to nearest matching catch/finally. Error classes capture messages and, in many environments, stacks. Promise rejections are async error channels, not caught by surrounding synchronous try/catch unless awaited.
language_semantics_records.syntax_or_api_shape: throw new Error(msg); try { } catch (e) { } finally { }
language_semantics_records.why_it_matters: Error handling must match sync, callback, promise, event, stream, and worker boundaries.
common_misuse: Catching too broadly and continuing with corrupt state
Throwing inside async callback expecting outer try/catch
safe_refactor_notes: Do not change throw to return error without API contract update
Use finally for cleanup, not normal result substitution
